assumptions: Claude Code only; behavior of the four surfaces is the host documentation as read on 2026-10-24 (changelog to 2.1.310) and is unconfirmed on a host until the probes HV-6 to HV-13 are recorded; the plugin MCP admission lock, worktree allowlist and limits are as in the repository; a declaration is a claim by the orchestrator and may be incomplete; settings are operator-owned; the G1 proposal was drafted by another track, is unfrozen and may change before the freeze; implementation follows #671, #672 and the pull request carrying this specification; SPEC-058 must exist as an unreleased engineering candidate before G1 arm A3 can run; EUR 0 additional spend on the founder's existing subscription.
compatibility: Additive. No change to agent_braid/analysis.py, AIM 0.2.0-draft, SPEC-023, the SPEC-052 gate and its schemas, the plugin MCP tools, limits or grants, or the existing five product skills. New: one pure module, four read-only CLI subcommands, schemas and a recipe document, all after #672 (the SPEC-052 implementation pull request). Any plugin-level change needs the ADR amendment handled by SPEC-058 and the SPEC-052 proposal.
domain: Declared ownership of 2 to 32 units on four documented Claude Code parallel surfaces (workflow-tracks, linked-sessions, agent-teams, batch) in Git repositories at file level, checked at committed or quiesced checkpoints and recovery points; not Codex, cloud or remote sessions, the VS Code extension, non-Git workspaces, or per-tool-call monitoring.
execution_contract: Read-only, local, offline and bounded. No model invocation, network, socket, launch, message, resume, stop, grant, merge or promotion by any command; no hook, mod, monitor, channel, workflow fan-out, skill or MCP tool is added; executionAuthorization is false in every emitted object; results are written only to explicit new private paths; probes are launched by the orchestrating session only after the founder authorizes each one, and G1 runs are started and approved by the founder, both outside this delivery; no concurrent agent, push or remote issue is authorized.
hypotheses: H-OR1 (untested; H-CW2 part a): on real Claude Code parallel runs a declared-ownership pre-flight plus a checkpoint receipt catches or prevents integration failures earlier than prompt partitioning plus the SPEC-052 gate without serializing most of the work. H-OR2 (untested; H-CW2 part a): the pre-flight false-assurance rate and the declaration under-coverage are small enough for the advice to be useful. H-CW2 part b (pull digests) is carried by SPEC-059 as H-LD1 and part c (opt-in guard) by SPEC-058 as H-OR3. Falsification and inconclusive outcomes are valid; the gates GA, GN and GG and their evaluation order are fixed in the G1 proposal.
observation_contract: Declaration records as written by the orchestrator; committed or quiesced Git state at named snapshots through the existing bounded Git adapter; documented host settings read from a closed key list of settings files; session state as printed by the host and supplied by the operator, used for booleans and counts only; host behavior only through recorded probe receipts of counts and booleans with the Claude Code version. Absent, unreadable or excluded observations are unknown or not-observed and never clean; an observation that cannot be taken in a bounded and stable way is a refusal (an error with a code and no result), not a result.

scenarios.given: any input to the new commands (declarations, Git state, `claude agents --json` output, settings files, script text)
scenarios.planned_evidence: tests/test_orchestration_bounds.py (planned, not existing) and procedure_req_017; exact commands, hashes, failures and limits are recorded when it runs. Planned only; obtained evidence: none. Tasks: T013, T018, T025, T040, T041, T042.
scenarios.then: all new commands are read-only, local and offline (no network and no socket); the commands refuse over-limit input before analysis (declaration at most 1 MiB, at most 32 units, at most 512 paths per unit, strings at most 256 characters, `claude agents --json` input at most 1 MiB, Git observation within the existing bounded Git helpers); the commands never write into the repository or the registry; the commands write results only to explicit new private paths and refuse existing paths; the commands store paths and hashes only (no file content, command text, prompts, transcripts, session names or settings values outside the closed key list); one rule governs every refusal: a busy lock, an unstable snapshot (a worktree that changes between the two Git observations), an unobservable source, an over-bound or malformed input and an existing output path end the command with a stable error code from a closed list (`command-error.schema.json`), a nonzero exit status and no result object, so that a refusal cannot appear as a receipt, a pre-flight verdict or a report and cannot be read as clean or independent, while `unknown`, `not-observed` and a recorded truncation inside a produced result are Article 13 outcomes of the observation contract and are also never clean (an observed list longer than its reporting bound is truncated and recorded, which is a result and not a refusal); and nothing is collected by telemetry now: the exclusion list below is part of this specification, and a later SPEC-047 vocabulary may add only the aggregate families named in task T041 after SPEC-047 and ADR 0025 are adopted and the producing feature ships
scenarios.when: the commands run, including on oversized, malformed or unreadable input

requirements.text: Fail closed within fixed bounds, refuse with errors and keep records free of content

scientific_limits: No acceptance evidence obtained and no host behavior observed. A declaration-based pre-flight is declared-only and no better than the declaration; disjoint declarations do not imply a clean merge; checkpoint receipts observe committed or quiesced file-level Git state only and not reads, Bash in flight or MCP effects; unattributed writers are unknown by default; hooks, if released later, cannot see Bash writes and fail open. The dogfood datum (three fan-outs, one stale-read event) is an anecdote with no measured outcome. The cited literature is mostly single-author preprints on research harnesses and none measures Claude Code surfaces. The prior-art pass bounds a wording, not a market fact, and unknown as a result is not a differentiator by itself. Structural tests prove no semantic or scientific claim. Hypotheses H-OR1 and H-OR2 may be false or inconclusive. No speed claim.
scope: Specify the advisory core of the Claude Code orchestration family for M4.6: a vendor-neutral ownership and footprint declaration with a pure expansion module, pre-flight evidence through the existing AIM analyzer, declared-versus-observed receipts at committed or quiesced checkpoints through the bundled CLI, an isolation and base audit, read-only recovery reports, epoch-stamped pull notices (the Mailbox of the default Mailbox + Whisper strategy), the orchestration-settings schema (most specific scope wins, block floor, operator-owned, versioned extension point, only the pull Mailbox effective), one refusal rule (errors with codes, never results), the policy-profile schema shared with SPEC-058, a per-surface capability and assurance matrix on one surface vocabulary, host-verification probes HV-6 to HV-13 launched by the orchestrating session after per-probe founder authorization, ownership of the preregistered and staged G1 protocol, documented and deferred interoperability inputs, a dated and repeatable prior-art pass with bounded wording, deferred orchestration skill and telemetry, and the governance boundary. SPEC-058 (opt-in guard, implemented first as an unreleased engineering candidate behind G1, adopted only with an ADR amendment after gate GG) and SPEC-059 (ledger and active push; reduced to a sketch of decisions and a draft coordination contract, with no requirement breakdown, blocked by G2 and its own ADR) are separate specifications.
